audit.why: 50.14% over 2537 games and the page's EVEN / 5.5-10 framing agree. Early lane is Aurora's because Siphon Power reaches 600 and Hextech Ray 525 against her 900 Q; the difficulty is entirely in the late game where Gravity Field's stun and a redirectable Arcane Storm own the ground she has to stand on.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text credits the 80s Arcane Storm cooldown to his augments. 80s is simply rank 3 of the ultimate (120/100/80), not an augment effect.
audit.why: Riot's ranked cooldown for Arcane Storm is 120/100/80. Glorious Evolution augments change the storm's move speed, not its cooldown.
audit.corrected: Attribute the 80s to rank 3 and keep the augment claim to what the kit text actually grants (Gravity Field slow on all his spells).

audit.whatIsWrong: The Siphon Power auto-attack reset — the actual visual tell that his combo has started — is stated nowhere on the page, and breakdown.trading is just tradeGood/tradeBad pasted together.
audit.why: Siphon Power (Q, 9/8/7/6/5s) both shields him and empowers his next basic attack, so his damage opens with an auto reset. The wind-up, not the cast, is the cue. Baiting that shield out before the Q-recast is the difference between a chunk and a whiff.
audit.corrected: breakdown.trading rewritten around the auto-reset tell and the 9s shield bait.

audit.why: The missingInteractions entry claims Arcane Storm is a channel that Aurora's R cancels. Riot's own description says the storm INTERRUPTS enemy channels — it is not itself a channel. The derived 'channel' flag misfired on that sentence, so the interaction was not written.
breakdown.cooldowns already carries real numbers: Gravity Field 17s, Hextech Ray 12s at 525, Siphon Power 9s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is a copy-paste bleed: the title says dodge his key line, the body talks about Gravity Field.
audit.why: His key line is Hextech Ray — 525 range, 12s at rank 1. The body must answer its own title.
audit.corrected: Body rewritten to the Hextech Ray sidestep during the Q recast.

edits.before: Good trade: Q the last-hit, E the step-up, Q-recast the slowed target, hop out — a full pattern he answered with a whiff. Bad trade: Hopping IN with W and trading while his engage is still loaded — the exit spent as an entrance is how Auroras get coached postmortem.
edits.after: His combo opens with a Siphon Power auto-reset, so the wind-up — not the cast — is your cue to step back. Bait that 9s shield out with a Q at 900, then land E and the recast into the gap; trade while it is down and his health bar has nothing absorbing your burst.

edits.before: Viktor burns Gravity Field on nothing — take the 17-second invitation and commit.
edits.after: Hextech Ray is a 525 line on 12s — sidestep it as you recast Q and his turn is spent.

edits.before: Full kit at 3 sets the pattern; level 6 adds the zone; Luden's makes the rotation half a bar.
edits.after: Full kit at 3 sets the pattern; 6 answers his 120s storm; Luden's beats his unaugmented core.

edits.before: Once his augments land and the AP stacks, Arcane Storm drops to an 80s cooldown and Gravity Field's stun holds you inside it, so his repeated zone damage outvalues your burst in grouped fights.
edits.after: Rank 3 Arcane Storm is an 80s cooldown he redirects onto you, and augmented Gravity Field slows through his whole rotation so the stun lands — his zone damage then outvalues your burst in grouped fights.

notes: Level chart (Aurora x6, Viktor at 2+ items) matches packet.levelChart and the whys — left alone. missingInteractions rule 'channel-interruptible' is a FALSE POSITIVE here: Riot's Arcane Storm text says it interrupts enemy channels, it is not a channel itself, so the 'your R cancels it' line was not written.
